articles.title: Pokémon card resellers have turned collecting into an online blood sport
articles.summary: Aftermarket card resellers are ruining the Pokémon fandom’s chances at getting their hands on valuable the 30th Celebration set.
articles.body: Earlier this month, Pokémon card content creator Natalie Roush posted a video to her YouTube and Instagram pages that enraged the larger collection community. In the now-deleted video, Roush shows off two premium boxes of cards that had not yet been officially released, and implores viewers not to be mad. But they were; other creators claimed that cards Roush had purchased were stolen from the manufacturer and mocked her for trying to sell them at exorbitant prices. The Roush situation was a high-profile example of the way Pokémon card collecting culture has been upended by the influencer economy and people trying to profit off the hobby. Though Roush has been relatively quiet in the days since the blowup, Pokémon collectors have been up in arms over a different — but very much related — problem. When the Pokémon Trading Card Game’s long-awaited 30th Celebration set finally released last week, collectors across the country lined up outside of stores in hopes of getting their hands on some shiny pieces of cardboard. The anniversary set has unusually strong pull rates — the rate at which you’re likely to find rare “chase” cards in a given set — giving more fans the cards they’ve always dreamed of, and potentially upsetting the aftermarket Poké-conomy. Some diehard Poké-fans even camped out overnight because a resurgence in popularity has made the cards much more difficult to find and buy in person. But another group of Pokémon card hunters was able to secure the highly sought-after set without having to travel to physical retailers or navigate the online Pokémon Center. [Media: Those people — resellers who often use automated bots to buy dozens of boxes of cards as soon as they’re available for preorder online — might not have had any intention of collecting the 30th Celebration set for themselves. But they have been trying to offload their spoils at marked-up prices to fans who haven’t had a chance to buy cards for themselves. Most retailers can’t keep cards on shelves, but there are plenty of videos online of resellers showing off piles of product they were able to obtain either by placing orders with bots or using inventory checking programs that alert them when brick-and-mortar stores receive stock. It’s also easy to find footage of resellers getting into altercations over cards, and in one recent instance, a 72-year-old man was arrested and charged with a first-degree misdemeanor for tracking a Pokémon delivery worker’s location with a device secretly planted in her car. Though flipping trading cards is nothing new, the Pokémon reselling economy has gotten much bigger in recent years as people have taken note of how durable the franchise’s popularity is. Many resellers like BotterBoyNova started off with other kinds of valuable merchandise before realizing that Pokémon products can be sold for far beyond the manufacturer’s suggested retail price, or MSRP. When I spoke with Nova recently, he told me that — like many millennials — he’s been a Pokémon fan since the mid-’90s. Nova was originally a content creator whose videos were mostly focused on reselling sneakers, but seeing how easy it was to profit from reselling Pokémon products convinced him that he needed to get in on the action. “Resellers in what’s described as the ‘Sneaker Twitter’ space are tapped in with practically every category of collectible that can resell for a profit,” Nova explained to me via Discord. “It’s not a situation where I’m singling out the Pokémon card market. It just so happens that it’s highly profitable and difficult to purchase for MSRP, and those are the conditions that our community specializes in.” [Media: Rather than operating independently, Nova works with Polar Chefs — a “cook group” community that sells monthly subscriptions to a variety of reseller tools and services. Subscriptions range from $660 per year to $75 per month, and they come with access to Polar Chefs’ private Discord server, restock alerts, and a selection of bots that can be used to buy cards. These bots make it easy for people to create multiple accounts on retailers’ websites that are attached to virtual credit cards, while the buyer’s IP address is spoofed with proxies. Technically, this kind of process isn’t illegal — at least not yet; Congress outlawed concert ticket-focused bots in 2016 and lawmakers have proposed doing the same for retail bots. But it does violate most retailers’ terms of service, which is why some resellers’ orders are canceled. Using Polar Chefs’ tools, Nova has been able to purchase massive amounts of Pokémon cards at MSRP from various retailers without being blocked by websites’ anti-bot security measures. Nova described his process of securing cards with bots as being “almost completely hands free,” and explained that the real work doesn’t begin until he has to sort and sell his inventory to a couple of bulk buyers. “During most weeks, I spend less than 3-5 hours a week on the reselling side of things (setting up bots, buying inventory, selling and fulfilling inventory),” Nova said, noting that he’s commonly asleep while pre-programmed bots make purchases for him. “I wait for notifications to come in from Polar Chefs which inform me of releases, bot adjustments I need to make, etc.” Though it is difficult to pinpoint exactly when Pokémon reselling really exploded in the past few years, the rise of groups like Polar Chefs feels reflective of the way that the creator economy evolved during the covid-19 pandemic. Resellers like Nova are influencers whose videos are designed to sell people on the idea that they could also be making money by flipping cards at scale. And monetized cook groups are prime examples of how online hustle culture has become more focused on the sale of how-to guides and courses for practices that can be seen as morally suspect. [Image: PASADENA, CALIFORNIA – SEPTEMBER 16: Pokémon card collectors wait in line outside a Best Buy store for a chance to purchase the new 30th Celebration set on September 16, 2026 in Pasadena, California. There’s an argument to be made that the scarcity created by resellers is part of what has driven the popularity of platforms like Whatnot — an online marketplace where people can pay for things like sealed Pokémon products, which are then opened on livestreams by the seller before they’re sent to the buyer. Many Whatnot streamers present themselves as entrepreneurs who are providing their audiences with a helpful service while also entertaining them. But the platform has been accused of operating more like an illegal gambling operation, and there is an entire ecosystem of creators whose content documents Whatnot streamers scamming their customers. But with the 30th Celebration packs flooding the market with rare cards, the scammers could be out of luck. Over the past week, X and Reddit have been inundated with screenshots from unnamed Discord servers where people claiming to be resellers appear to be melting down over not being able to sell their overpriced cards. One of the more widely circulated images features a person insisting that resellers are “the people that actually ensure [The Pokémon Company] makes money,” while complaining that “there’s literally no value in these sets because everyone can pull the rare bullshit.” In another, a reseller says they are filing a class action lawsuit against The Pokémon Company “for independent vendors who suffered severe financial asset devaluation due to artificial market saturation.” [Media: The absurdity of these posts suggests that they might have been written by people making fun of actual resellers, as does the fact that while searching Discord I found some posts that use the exact same wording. Those posters might have just been looking for attention, but the state of the larger reselling economy does seem to be having a negative impact on Pokémon cards’ availability. Even though The Pokémon Company is printing more cards than ever, almost everything about the modern aftermarket economy has made it harder for ordinary people — especially children — to participate in the hobby. Nova told me that he thinks casual collectors who just want to pull cool cards for themselves are completely justified in feeling that resellers are making Pokémon less accessible. He also believes that collectors whose interest in the cards is “incentivized by monetary gain” are hypocrites for taking issue with resellers. Aside from actually playing with them, the real fun of Pokémon cards is in the hunt and delight when you’re able to find a pack that shocks you with its contents. It’s an experience everyone’s supposed to be able to enjoy, but it’s being ruined by hustlers.

articles.title: Control Resonant is a great game — it’s even better when you read everything
articles.summary: ﻿There’s a lot to read in Remedy’s Control sequel, even just in the menus. It’s worth taking the time to pore over it all.
articles.body: In Control Resonant, the entire world is at stake. But that didn’t stop the diligent employees of the Federal Bureau of Control from filing reams of paperwork, and it didn’t stop me from reading everything I could find, either. Reading is often optional in Resonant, but it’s where some of the game’s best details — and even love stories! — can be found. In the world of Control Resonant and its predecessor, 2019’s Control, the FBC deals with mysterious, otherworldly objects and entities that defy explanation. But the FBC itself is still an old-school bureaucratic agency, and that means tons of (often heavily redacted) reports and memos and miscellaneous bits of paper to sort through. I like reading, and I especially like reading Remedy’s clever and often funny writing, but I was overwhelmed at first by the sheer amount of text. Initially I skipped documents that seemed optional: the enemy logs, which are compiled in a separate tab and unlocked automatically after fighting each enemy type for the first time. I was kind of busy just learning how to get around — I’m not the best at spatial reasoning in general, and gravity doesn’t always matter in Resonant’s M.C. Escher-ified version of Manhattan. I was also too busy beating down the game’s many Hiss and mold enemies to read about them. [Image: The game’s best documents contain valuable info about the world as well as the personalities of the people in it. But I was having enough trouble with combat early on that I eventually decided to read through the enemy logs I’d unlocked to see if they’d be any help. (There’s an assist mode so you can tweak the combat difficulty, but I was feeling too stubborn to use it. Remedy has since deployed a hotfix to address criticisms of the combat balance.) The logs, compiled by the FBC’s “Threat Assessment Team,” did actually help; they detail each enemy’s attack patterns and weaknesses, which aren’t always easy to figure out when they come at you in large groups. But I was delighted to find that the enemy logs also hide a workplace romantic comedy. The Threat Assessment Team consists of Rick Patel, who documents the Hiss, and Lydia M.B. McPierce, who documents the mold and some later-game enemies. Rick is pretty serious and straightforward, whereas Lydia finds lots of time to talk shit about the mold in between her regular notes. Opposites attract, though. Across dozens of logs, I saw their individual personalities unfold — as well as the beginning of their love story. One of the enemies, the Hiss Transporter, is a city bus that’s been corrupted by the Hiss and sends out drones to attack on its behalf. In his log about it, Rick describes the dynamic between the bus and its drones — which are seemingly once-human Hiss entities fused to bus seats — as “motherly.” Lydia calls him out on this in a separate document about a mold enemy called the Spore Mother. “(For the record, I was not the one who named this one ‘mother,’ that was Rick. I went to therapy and did the work precisely so I wouldn’t feel the urge to do that),” she writes in an aside at the bottom. In another document, Lydia teases Rick, who she’s calling “Ricky” at this point, about beating him at chess and challenges him to a rematch. [Image: Lydia is sassing Rick a little, but she obviously likes how much he cares! Lydia is one of the best examples in Resonant of how funny Remedy’s writing can be, while Rick is much drier. But he’s also sweet and references Lydia often; in one log, he says that had he realized Lydia had emetophobia, he would’ve offered to trade some responsibilities with her so she could avoid the vomit-like attacks of the mold. (I have emetophobia myself, so I found this especially charming. Good on Ricky.) Then, in a document about a particularly dangerous Hiss variant that he came too close to during his observations, Rick finally lays it all bare: > I could have died. Another close call like that and it might just be the end for me. I don’t want to go without taking a chance on us, Lydia. Remember how we laughed at our ideal dates being the exact opposites of each other, how chaotic a pair we’d make? It doesn’t have to be just a joke. I think we could have something real together, you and I. What do you think? (Don’t worry, you can tell me over coffee what a coward I am for not doing this in person.) I’m not sure if Lydia has actually seen this note, because I’m still missing one singular enemy log. But I know she likes him back. In a late-game document, as the world is really looking doomed, Lydia adds an aside at the bottom: “(Hey Ricky, this is out of left field, but if we actually survive this, wanna grab a coffee sometime?)” Remedy seeds little stories and fun details like these throughout the world of Resonant, not just in written documents. But reading, it turns out, was integral to my experience. I learned how to fight the game’s enemies a little better, and in the process, I was endeared to two characters I never actually met. There’s also a lot more to discover than just office romance — everything from an influencer’s view of Manhattan’s “inception ahh streets” to the FBC’s serious ethics violations — and so much of it enriches Remedy’s fantastically weird world. I’m now determined to track down and kill that last enemy type so I can read Lydia’s final log, and I’m sure I’ll stumble upon some other documents I missed along the way. I can’t wait to see what I find.

articles.summary: Score early Amazon Prime Big Deal Days savings on Philips Sonicare electric toothbrushes in the UK, from the budget-friendly 2100 Series to the premium DiamondClean Prestige.
articles.body:
Amazon's Prime Big Deal Days doesn't officially begin until October 6, but we're already seeing some early discounts ahead of the two-day shopping event, including savings across Philips' Sonicare electric toothbrush range.

There are several models currently reduced at Amazon UK, ranging from the more affordable Sonicare 2100 Series to the considerably fancier DiamondClean Prestige 9900. So, whether you're looking to make the switch from a manual toothbrush or simply fancy upgrading your current one, there are a few options worth checking out before Prime Big Deal Days properly gets underway.

Philips Sonicare 2100 Series Electric Toothbrush

The Philips Sonicare 2100 Series is currently £44 at Amazon UK, making it the cheapest option in this particular selection and a relatively straightforward entry point if you've never used an electric toothbrush before.

It delivers 31,000 bristle movements per minute and has two intensity settings, Medium and Low, alongside a programme designed to ease you into using an electric toothbrush over your first week.

There's also a two-minute timer to help you brush for the recommended amount of time, while Philips says the battery can last for up to 14 days between charges.

Philips Sonicare DiamondClean 9000 Series

If you want something a little more premium, the Sonicare DiamondClean 9000 is currently £119.99.

This model offers four brushing modes, including Clean, Deep Clean+, Gum Health and White+, alongside Philips' more advanced cleaning technology. Philips also claims it can remove up to 10 times more plaque than a manual toothbrush and help remove surface stains for whiter-looking teeth.

You also get a travel case, which is a nice inclusion if you're the sort of person who doesn't fancy throwing an electric toothbrush loose into your luggage.

Philips Sonicare DiamondClean Prestige 9900

This is the most advanced and expensive option of the bunch, using Philips' SenseIQ technology to monitor pressure, motion and coverage up to 100 times per second. It can then adjust the brushing experience accordingly, with the aim of keeping things consistent and comfortable.

Philips claims the Prestige 9900 can provide up to 20 times more plaque removal than a manual toothbrush, so you're getting into properly premium electric toothbrush territory here.

It's worth stressing that these aren't Prime Big Deal Days prices just yet. Amazon's main October shopping event runs October 6-7 , meaning there's still time for these prices to change, potentially in either direction.

That said, if you've been meaning to upgrade your toothbrush anyway, you don't necessarily need to wait until October 6. There are already several Sonicare models discounted ahead of the event, and the cheaper options in particular could make sense if you simply want to ditch the manual toothbrush without spending a small fortune.

articles.title: Werwulf Director Robert Eggers Reveals New Details About His 'Hell-Like' Medieval Horror Film
articles.summary: Director Robert Eggers reveals eerie new details about Werwulf, his upcoming medieval horror film starring Aaron Taylor-Johnson, Willem Dafoe and Lily-Rose Depp.
articles.body:
“After Nosferatu, I kind of said, ‘Let me try to write the scariest thing I can write.’ I don't know that I did that, but I definitely wrote the darkest thing,” writer-director Robert Eggers told the press at a promotional event Friday for his upcoming horror film, Werwulf. And based on the roughly 20 minutes of select footage I saw from the film, Werwulf indeed has all the makings of being Eggers’ darkest and scariest movie yet.

Werwulf follows a 13th-century farmer (Aaron Taylor-Johnson), simply referred to as Man, who is cursed as a werewolf. Lily-Rose Depp plays his wife and the mother of his children, while Willem Dafoe, Ralph Ineson, and Jack Morris play a trio of wolf hunters on a mission to kill the werewolf.

Eggers kicked the event off by screening the opening scene of Werwulf, a dialogue-free nighttime sequence. The howling of wolves can be heard over a black screen. Then the Man’s face is revealed. He is foaming at the mouth and in great pain. The Man sprints naked through the woods and enters an empty home. Inside, he suffers wild convulsions in the moonlight and growls in agony. He writhes on the floor, and eventually ends up in the shadows where his transformation continues unseen. Taylor-Johnson performed all these body-bending movements himself (save for one shot that could not be accomplished practically), and it was truly a wild sight to behold. Eggers stressed, though, “that is not the set piece werewolf transformation.”

“I think werewolf movies are a difficult genre. And I think sometimes even if it's a great werewolf movie, it's hard to believe that your dad's turning into a werewolf or your next door neighbor who's a high school basketball player is turning into a werewolf,” Eggers said. But a period werewolf movie “really helps ground you and ground the audience. At least that's the intention.”

While I won’t give blow-by-blow details of the other scenes in order to avoid spoilers, the additional footage showed: aspects of the Man’s youth; hints at how and why he ended up cursed; the arrival of three wolf hunters at the Man’s home in the middle of the night to violently enlist his help in hunting down a werewolf; and the Man and the hunters’ journey to find a strange old woman who may know a thing or two about werewolves.

Eggers did copious amounts of research on England in the 13th century for the screenplay, he co-wrote with his The Northman collaborator, Sjón. The film’s dialogue is in Middle English, although it’s been altered by dialect coach William Conacher to make it more comprehensible for the modern ear. Eggers also worked with two Middle English scholars at Oxford University, Eleanor Baker and Daniel Wakelin , who helped make the dialogue more period accurate.

Although the dialogue is in Middle English, Eggers said that Werwulf “was designed to be kind of like a silent movie. You don't need to understand what anyone's saying to understand the movie because you're with everyone on an emotional level, particularly Aaron and his family.”

Eggers’ fascination with werewolf lore goes back to this youth. “The historical werewolves that I had read about starting in high school, they were doing things that were so taboo and hard for anyone to wrap their mind around because it was so extreme that the culture that they existed in said, ‘You can't be a human, you must be a werewolf.’ So it was going to be very dark and very primal subject matter,” the filmmaker said.

“I wanted to make it in England and because Edward I was trying to protect the wool trade around the time of this movie, he set a campaign to exterminate all the wolves. Actually, Willem's character is based on a real person who did such a good job that in another 200 years there were not wolves in England. So without wolves, you don't have werewolf lore. So if I was going to set it in England, it had to be this early in history around 1300. And that was even more exciting, because the world would be so primitive and so visceral and primal that that would make this all the more dark and brutal.”

The world of Werwulf is so dark and brutal that Eggers’ said cinematographer Jarin Blaschke texted him after he first read the script and asked, "’Does this take place in hell?’ And it needs to be hell for Aaron. And I think some medievalists would be annoyed that I'm kind of clinging to the stereotype of the Middle Ages being so muddy and dirty and rainy and miserable, but it needs to be so muddy, and rainy, and dirty, and miserable, and shit-covered, and it does need to be hell. But again, I always find that doing the research about the period, you learn stuff that makes it more interesting and more specific. And for this particular movie, more hell-like.”

Audiences will discover for themselves just how hell-like Werwulf is when it opens in theaters Christmas Day.

articles.title: John Goodman, Laura Bailey, and Ian Alexander to Star in HBO's The Last of Us Season 3
articles.summary: Emmy-winning actor John Goodman, prolific voice talent Laura Bailey, and returning star Ian Alexander have been cast in the third (and possibly final) season of HBO’s The Last of Us series.
articles.body:
Emmy-winning actor John Goodman, prolific voice talent Laura Bailey, and returning star Ian Alexander have been cast in the third (and possibly final) season of HBO’s The Last of Us series.

As revealed on September 26 — the day the Cordyceps infection ravaged humanity in The Last of Us universe — the show’s third season will feature three big talents, two of whom are making their return to Naughty Dog’s flagship zombie franchise.

Perhaps most surprisingly, John Goodman has been slated to play a character named Joey, a figure who wasn’t in the original games. Joey is joined by another character named Paco, who will be played by Ian Alexander; the two are described as a “friendly duo who dub themselves ‘Heroes of the Highway.’” Alexander notably played Lev in The Last of Us Part 2 , a young boy who Abby helps rescue from the Seraphite cult.

The Last of Us Season 2 Episode 1: TV Show vs Game Comparison

The Seraphites will play a part in season 3, as Laura Bailey is set to play Elizabeth, one of the cult’s leaders. Bailey is also a returning actor to the franchise, having famously voiced Abby in The Last of Us Part 2 alongside Alexander.

With the Seraphites being included in the third season and Alexander playing a new character, it stands to reason that another person will be playing Lev, most likely because Alexander has aged out of the role.

These two aren’t the only actors from the original games who have been included in HBO’s screen adaptation; Ashley Johnson and Troy Baker also played characters in The Last of Us Season 1, with Johnson playing Ellie’s mother in a harrowing birth scene and Baker playing James, a member of Baker’s villainous group.

Johnson and Baker famously provided the voice and motion performances for Ellie and Joel in both of The Last of Us Games, so it’s not surprising that Bailey and Alexander are also showing up in some way.

HBO’s The Last of Us series is expected to end with this forthcoming season, which will air in 2027. In a September interview with Deadline, the Chairman and CEO of HBO and Max Content, Casey Bloys, said he “thinks [showrunner] Craig [Mazin] has planned it as the final season.”

Bloys has been hinting at this since January, saying in another Deadline interview that “it certainly seems that way, but on decisions like that, we will defer to the showrunners. So you can ask them.”

With the games’ creator, Niel Druckmann, having left the project after Season 2, the future of HBO’s show is looking uncertain — but with talent like Alexander, Bailey, and Goodman on board, there’s bound to be some fantastic performances in store. We just hope they don’t tear our hearts apart like Nick Offerman did in the first season.

articles.body:
In the aftermath of yet another price hike , Disney has revealed next month’s streaming lineup for both Disney+ and Hulu.

Why are we talking about both streaming services at the same time? Over the past year, Disney+ and Hulu have been slowly merging their libraries . They also cost about the same as a bundle as they would as individual standalone services, presumably by design.

If you’re debating whether to stick with the more expensive subscriptions, here’s a look ahead at what you’ll be getting out of it next month. The topline? We’re looking at a new MCU series, tons of ABC show premieres, and plenty of Halloween specials.

Highlights Coming to Disney+ and Hulu Next Month

One of the most anticipated TV streaming premieres is a new season of Ryan Murphy’s fever dream, American Horror Story. Plenty of cast members have returned for the hauntingly significant 13th season, including Sarah Paulson, Evan Peters, Angela Bassett, and Emma Roberts. In other words, expect some wacky crossovers of characters and plotlines from previous seasons.

While the first three episodes premiered on FX in late September, they won’t be coming to Hulu until the start of October. Time to get spooky.

The Hunger Games movies have moved around streaming services quite a bit over the years. Having all of the movies in one place is a great chance to catch up on or rewatch the dystopian saga ahead of a new prequel movie, Sunrise on the Reaping .

The biggest Disney+ premiere of the month comes from the MCU side of things. VisionQuest is a new series that follows up 2017’s WandaVision, one of the most acclaimed Marvel projects in the streaming era. Between last year’s Weapons and this year’s Resident Evil , Zach Cregger has been having quite a run. We’d argue that the run started with the director’s debut movie, Barbarian. Last but not least, it’s definitely worth keeping an eye out for Halloween specials.

Family Guy is already confirmed to be dropping its special episode on October 5, while Phineas & Ferb have a Halloween episode slated for October 7. articles.title: Melissa Barrera Says She Would Reprise Her Scream Role, Reveals Conditions for Her Return
articles.summary: Actress Melissa Barrera said she is open to returning to Scream, but don't expect to see her reprise her role as Sam Carpenter as long as Spyglass Media has the rights.
articles.body:
Actress Melissa Barrera said she is open to returning to Scream, but don't expect to see her reprise her role as Sam Carpenter as long as Spyglass Media has the rights.

The Scream 5 and Scream 6 star opened up about what it would take to bring her back to Wes Craven's legendary slasher franchise during an interview with JustWatch . Barrera explained that she still "loves the franchise," but the people overseeing it are what's keeping her from going another round with Ghostface.

"Not with the company that currently holds the rights," she said when asked if she would return if she got a call to reprise her role. "I love the franchise. I had an amazing time making those movies, but a lot of the hate and difficulty that I've faced in the last years is because the leadership of that company made it a point to label me something that I'm not."

"And they never apologized, even when I was proven right. Even with an apology, I wouldn't go back to work with them – not that I'm holding my breath. I don't think they have that ability."

Barrera starred in two installments for the horror franchise and was set to return for a third run with Jenna Ortega but was fired by Spyglass following a series of pro-Palestine social media posts she published in late 2023 . At the time, Spyglass said it has "zero tolerance for antisemitism or the incitement of hate."

"I pray day and night for no more deaths, for no more violence, and for peaceful co-existence," Barrera said in a statement following her firing. "I will continue to speak out for those that need it most and continue to advocate for peace and safety, for human rights and freedom. Silence is not an option for me."

The Scream rights holder's move was immediately met with backlash from fans for more reasons than one. Barrera had helped bring the franchise back to theaters after a decade without a new installment, and when she was unceremoniously removed as the lead of Scream 7 , other talent happened to follow suit. Jenna Ortega departed Scream 7 just weeks after it all went down. Director Christopher Landon confirmed his exit just one month after Spyglass fired Barrera.

Paramount Pictures and Spyglass went on to release a very different vision for the franchise when Scream 7 premiered earlier this year. Although familiar faces helped it break records at the box office , the latest entry debuted to franchise-low reviews, as shared by Rotten Tomatoes . IGN gave it a 6/10 . Scream 8 is also reportedly in the works.

Despite veering off in a completely new direction, Barrera said now that she's open to coming back. For her, it's not just about working under new management but honoring Craven's legacy.

"If the franchise were ever to leave those hands and go into hands that would, I think, honor Wes Craven's legacy more… I think, yeah," she continued regarding her interest in a return to the franchise.

For now, Barrera remains uninvolved with Scream. Series star Matthew Lillard recently spoke up about his surprise return in Scream 7. During a recent Q&A (via Deadline ), he said he was "embarrassed" to have reprised his role.

" I’m just gonna say, what happened to Melissa, the whole world didn’t pipe up," he said. "She was like a year early on what the f**k’s going on, but the whole world should have piped up and said, ‘she’s right,’ and they didn’t. And that’s brutal."

For now, Scream 8 has no release date. Although ideas for the next film are something that have been in the works behind the scenes for some time , there's no information about who may show up in it.

articles.title: Starring Jacob Tremblay and Russell Crowe, Netflix’s Unabomber Struggles to Turn Ted Kaczynski’s Origin Story Into a Compelling Thriller
articles.summary: Unabomber covers the formative years and later arrest of Ted Kaczynski, the titular mail bomber who terrorized the US from the late 1970s until the mid-1990s. Director Janus Metz’s mixed bag of a film aims to understand the origin of a domestic terrorist but it never quite convinces or connects.
articles.body:
Unabomber covers the formative years and later arrest of Ted Kaczynski, the titular mail bomber who terrorized the US from the late 1970s until the mid-1990s. Director Janus Metz’s mixed bag of a film aims to understand the origin of a domestic terrorist but it never quite convinces or connects.

As FBI Agent Joanne Miller, Shailene Woodley — decent in a two-dimensional role almost any actress could have played — leads the surprisingly inert 1990s portions of the film chronicling the manhunt for Kaczynski, then a hermit living in the woods of Montana.

This storyline strives for serial killer movie suspense, but it never musters enough thrills to overcome its inherent tropes. It reduces the FBI’s capture to a dull TV cop procedural instead of capturing the magnitude of what was a historic win for law enforcement.

What sets Unabomber apart from other projects about this notorious criminal are the portions set at Harvard University during the Cold War. This is where teenage Theodore Kaczynski (Jacob Tremblay), a brilliant mathematics student who yearns to be a philosopher, participates in a harrowing psychological experiment overseen by Professor Henry Murray (Russell Crowe).

Murray’s (now clearly unethical) program was meant to stress-test a person’s philosophical arguments, but instead it became an abusive quest to break a person until they changed. (It’s all very Manchurian Candidate .)

The movie suggests that Murray ultimately unleashed a monster within Kaczynski who would later target the industrial and academic institutions he blamed for ruining the natural world and robbing humans of liberty. The reality is more complicated .

As the prodigy-era Kaczynski, Tremblay, try as he might, struggles to convey the psychological layers of his damaged character. Crowe delivers a fine but rote turn as the doctor who manipulated his student.

Murray’s actions certainly make him the heavy of this film, but Crowe plays him with enough haughtiness to prevent the character from being a complete mad scientist cliche. Like Kaczynski, Murray wants the world to know how brilliant he is but he may, in fact, just be a big loser.

If you’re on Netflix looking for something worth your while about this subject the better choice to stream would be the 2020 documentary Unabomber: In His Own Words.

articles.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Extended Clip Reveals Closer Look at Ganondorf
articles.summary: Nintendo has published a short clip that shows a closer look at Ganondorf in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake.
articles.body:
Nintendo has published a short clip that shows a closer look at Ganondorf in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake .

Those who have the Nintendo Today! app downloaded on their mobile devices were treated to more footage from the upcoming reimagining yesterday. The video in question is, crushingly, only 16 seconds long, but it reveals an extended look at how The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is reincarnating one of video games' most iconic villains for Nintendo Switch 2.

"A man from the Gerudo, a tribe in which men are said to be born only once in a hundred years," official text shared by Nintendo said. "He harbors a grand ambition to obtain the Triforce, a sacred relic rumored to grant the wish of any individual who touches it."

GANONDORF IN THE NEW SNEAK PEAK FOR OCARINA OF TIME??? holy shit he's so cool pic.twitter.com/Q85Im9XA6Y — bea (@SlLENTPRINCESS) September 25, 2026

GANONDORF IN THE NEW SNEAK PEAK FOR OCARINA OF TIME??? holy shit he's so cool pic.twitter.com/Q85Im9XA6Y

We first saw how Ganondorf would fit into the remake's divisive art style when Nintendo unveiled gameplay during its dedicated Direct earlier this month. The new footage expands on the updated dream sequence shown previously, showing the evildoer riding on horseback as voiceover says, "And now… An evil has appeared, yearning after that power."

While technically a scene players have already been looking at for decades, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake will alter the moment with more than just shiny new graphics, even if the changes are small. As highlighted in the Nintendo Today! post, while the extended clip shows that the Switch 2 version of the scene is running in slow motion, the original Nintendo 64 and 3DS remake versions show Ganondorf moving like normal.

Again, it's an extremely small change, but it's also yet another sign that the November reimagining will come with a few tweaks to a classic that fans may want to prepare themselves for. It all arrives as fans continue to be torn about some of the promised tweaks, just as a dedicated jump button, while Nintendo chose to intentionally retain the loading screens from the original experience .

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake launches for Switch 2 November 5, 2026. For more, you can read about the time Ubisoft reportedly scrapped a Zelda spinoff with Ganondorf as the protagonist . You can also learn about how Shigeru Miyamoto's love for puppetry may have influenced the remake's art style .

articles.title: Minecraft Confirms Ice Caves as Next Game Drop, Adds Frozen Zombies, Ice Balls, and More
articles.summary: Mojang has teased Minecraft’s next game drop, giving fans a sneak peek at some of its features.
articles.body:
Mojang has teased Minecraft’s next game drop, giving fans a sneak peek at some of its features.

As revealed at Minecraft LIVE, Ice Caves are coming to the game, adding a new and rare underground extension of cold biomes with glowing ice crystals and environmental variety. Ice Caves include a new hostile mob, the frozen zombie, which can apply freezing effects and throw damaging ice balls. The ice balls can also be used as weapons or to craft potions, adding strategic options for combat scenarios.

Mojang said Ice Caves add a whole new layer of variety to cold biomes, making exploring underground even more interesting, thanks to the increased environmental diversity. “Though they may be beautiful, these caves are far from safe,” the developer said.

Ice crystals can be found in ice caves and can be placed both vertically and horizontally, providing lots of potential for decoration and building. They can even be used as a light source. The Frozen Zombie, meanwhile, applies a stacking freezing effect with its melee attacks. If you take enough hits, you'll freeze. It also throws ice balls at you, which apply knockback and deal damage. Normal zombies can convert into Frozen when exposed to powder snow. Players can already convert Husks into Zombies, and now Zombies into Frozen, opening the door for advanced mob farms.

Frozen drop ice balls on death, allowing players to use them as well, but they can also be crafted and used to brew a new potion. As a weapon, ice balls deal damage and apply knockback, and as a potion it can freeze players.

articles.body:
Naughty Dog has released a free background on PlayStation 5 as it prepares to celebrate The Last of Us Day 2026.

The studio behind Sony's exclusive post-apocalyptic video game franchise took to social media to tease some of what it has planned for this year's festivities. While September 26 is technically the day it's chosen to serve as its Cordyceps-breakout holiday, Naughty Dog won't share any The Last of Us announcements with fans until Monday the 28th, but that doesn't mean there's nothing to fawn over today.

PS5 owners can now head to their consoles to download a special The Last of Us-themed background for PlayStation's Welcome Hub landing page. It's a free option featuring both the younger and older versions of Ellie from both mainline games, with no download required to enjoy it. Although it's far from the kind of dynamic themes or wallpapers fans have begged Sony to bring back, the animated background does add some flavor for fans still hoping to see the series get a proper return in games.

Those who want to spice up their PS5 backgrounds need only to navigate to the Welcome Hub, select the Change Background button in the top corner of the screen, and then select The Last of Us background in the Games tab. There will also be a No Return charity stream on Twitch.

Another surprise announced today was the news that The Last of Us Season 3 on HBO has picked up some new and familiar faces : John Goodman, Laura Bailey, and Ian Alexander. Goodman, a series newcomer and award-winning actor, will play a new character named Joey. Bailey, who played Abby in The Last of Us Part 2 and a nurse in The Last of Us Season 1, will play a Seraphite leader named Elizabeth, while Alexander will play a currently unnamed character after first appearing as Lev in the second game.

We'll have to wait to see what Naughty Dog has planned for The Last of Us Day 2026. While Sony has yet to confirm a The Last of Us Part 3 as work on its Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet continues, fans are hoping an announcement will arrive sooner rather than later . One comment from creator Neil Druckmann sparked theories about a third chapter in Ellie's story in March of this year .

articles.title: Everything Coming to Peacock in October
articles.body:
Peacock is going all-in on horror this month. A ton of scary movies are getting added to the service starting on October 1, including major franchises like Scream and Friday the 13th.

Speaking of Friday the 13th, Peacock is also dropping a new original prequel called Crystal Lake on October 15. The highly anticipated series follows Jason's mother who is still mourning nearly a year after his death.

If you're wondering what's worth watching, we've gathered together some of our top picks right here. You can also jump to all of the new releases for October for the full list by day.

Although Marvel's upcoming Blade movie has been tragically cancelled , the original trilogy is still ripe for the watching. After Wesley Snipes' cameo in Deadpool & Wolverine , the films have been harder to find. The trilogy being added to streaming service is worthy of a movie marathon celebration, especially during the spooky season. The second Blade is arguably one of the best vampire movies ever made after all.

Although The Mummy isn't the scariest of movies, it's still worth a rewatch in October. This is arguably the best Brendan Fraser movies of all time and the franchise is set to get its fourth installment in October 2027. Fraser has been reportedly training for the upcoming movie, which is bringing back many of the original characters that made it such a timeless classic.

Train to Busan is a Korean zombie apocalypse movie that does everything right. The story follows a businessman named Seo Seok-woo and his daughter as they travel on a train to Busan that is actively being overrun by vicious zombies. If you don't mind watching a film with subtitles, we highly recommend checking it out. Train to Busan currently sits on our list of the best zombie movies of all time .

It's been 17 years since the last Friday the 13th movie was released, so right now feels like the perfect time for a new addition to the franchise. Crystal Lake is a prequel series that focuses on the events before the original 1980 movie that started it all. The story follows Jason's mother, who is still dealing with the aftermath of her son's death. The series will offer a fresh look at the events and people that helped make one of the most iconic horror villains of all time.

articles.title: Microsoft CEO Says 'Streamlining' at Xbox is 'Great to See' as Layoffs Affect Thousands
articles.summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has spoken about the state of Xbox following layoffs that affected thousands of workers, saying that the "streamlining" at the company is "great to see."
articles.body:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has spoken about the state of Xbox following layoffs that affected thousands of workers, saying that the "streamlining" at the company is "great to see."

The tech executive opened up about how the business' gaming branch is doing during a recent interview on the Sources Podcast with Alex Heath . It's a conversation that followed not only the 1,600 job cuts Xbox delivered in July of this year but also the additional structural changes that were announced just this past week.

When touching on Xbox's place under the grander Microsoft umbrella, Nadella said he feels "fantastic" about the IP the brand has in its portfolio and its "ability to take that and produce great games going forward." As layoffs continue to reshape the developers who have made some of those great games, he still seems to be feeling pretty good.

"There's a certain amount of streamlining the team is doing and [Xbox CEO Asha Sharma] is doing, which is great to see," Nadella said in the wake of the most recent cuts. "And then, we have to invent the right sustainable business model that allows us to deliver gaming to more and more people.

"That has always been the goal, which is, we want to be a great publisher and a great platform provider for games across both PCs and Xboxes. So, that is our goal, and I think Asha and team have said that Xbox is going to get back to growth this next fiscal year, and that's the plan they're executing on, and in that process, do a bang-up job of producing some great games."

It's optimism that may come as a shock to those who have watched as Microsoft continues to redefine what the Xbox name means by shedding game developers like Double Fine and Ninja Theory and reorganizing beloved studios like id Software . Maybe the most telling sign that the company is entering a new chapter arrived just this past week, when it announced that Halo would be moved from Halo Studios to its Activision teams.

Xbox announced in July that it could be laying off 1,600 staff, with an additional 1,600 set to follow before the end of the fiscal year. Although this past week offered a closer look at what that long-term plan entails, we won't know the full scope of the company's big "reset" initiative for at least a few more months.

For now, the resulting changes also include the Fallout: New Vegas team at Obsidian Entertainment moving under Bethesda . After State of Decay developer Undead Labs confirmed its independence just days ago, studio head Philip Holt told IGN that the zombie series' third game remains in active development amid its own "significant" wave of layoffs.

For more on how the industry has changed in recent months, you can read about what Nadella had to say about how Xbox's monetization plan at Microsoft compares to YouTube . You can also catch up on what he said about the brand when former Xbox CEO Phil Spencer departed the company .

articles.title: Godzilla Minus Zero Brings Scenes of Breathtaking Destruction and Terror, and Yet Something Is Still Missing From the Film
articles.summary: Review: Godzilla Minus Zero doesn’t disappoint in the slightest on the kaiju front, but does lack the same level of emotional resonance that its predecessor held.
articles.body:
This review is based on a screening timed to the New York Film Festival. Godzilla Minus Zero opens in theaters in Japan on November 3 and in North America on November 6.

Godzilla movies have long had a problem: What do you do after the initial thrill of a quote/unquote serious Godzilla origin story? Can the filmmakers somehow continue the deep thematic underpinnings of that first adventure, even while upping the visual ante with more giant monster action? How do you offer a probing commentary about the world we live in – which is what the best of the genre is known for – when you’ve got skyscraper-sized lizards slugging it out MMA-style?

It is under these circumstances – or should I say restrictions? – that Godzilla Minus Zero enters the ring. As the sequel to the much-praised Godzilla Minus One from three years ago – a picture that dealt with, among other things, notions of survivor’s guilt, hope in the face of hopelessness, found family, and more – Minus Zero is on the ropes from the start. Can returning writer-director Takashi Yamazaki wring even more out of his characters, who have already been to hell and back, while also blowin’ up stuff real good? In a word, no.

The film takes place two years after the events of Minus One, with Ryunosuke Kamiki back as Kōichi Shikishima and Minami Hamabe returning as Noriko. Kōichi, as fans of the Oscar-winning previous movie (for Best Visual Effects) will remember, is the former would-be kamikaze pilot from World War II who was instrumental in defeating Godzilla the first time around. Now married to Noriko, the woman he took in after the American air raids on Tokyo, the pair have also adopted Akiko, the orphaned baby they had cared for after that same disaster. Living happily together as a family, there’s only one thing that can ruin this idyllic picture… well, two things, since not only is Godzilla of course back, but there’s a new monster on the scene as well.

Minus Zero opens with a sequence of devastation, as this new critter lays waste to countless helpless civilians as they flee in the streets, avoiding both falling rubble from the buildings crumbling around them and lightning breath from the creature’s mouth. Yes, as fans have already figured out and as the marketing for the film has teased , this is Ghidorah, also known as King Ghidorah in the larger Toho mythology, and generally the archnemesis of the big guy for whom we have all gathered once again. (Ghidorah has also been referred to as “Monster Zero,” which helps to explain this film’s title.)

These scenes of destruction and terror are breathtaking, with Yamazaki and his team of visual effects maestros once again managing to keep their creatures from feeling like CGI monstrosities. No, rather, Ghidorah, and Godzilla when he eventually shows up too, just appear to be real monstrosities – humongous, slow-moving, reptile-like, and all-the more terrifying for it. Ghidorah also distinguishes himself from his counterpart with his scary yet herky-jerky, almost cat-like mannerisms.

So as soon as that first-round bell rings, the movie has already proven its VFX bona fides – to no one’s surprise. But it has also confirmed that a Godzilla Part 2 inevitably means more monsters. And look, none of this is to say that there’s anything wrong with a movie where Godzilla has to rip his own arm off because his foe’s teeth are sunk so tightly into it. We all love monster-on-monster action, but there’s no denying that the more of a mash a monster movie becomes – be it of the Toho, Universal, Alien/Xenomorph, or whatever else variety – the more it loses its edge as the human characters and their emotional baggage run the risk of looking puny in the face of these god-like creatures.

Remember what Bogart said in Casablanca? “It doesn't take much to see that the problems of three little people don't amount to a hill of beans in this crazy world.” Yes, I’m quoting Humphrey Bogart in a Godzilla review, but if there’s an issue with Minus Zero, it’s that the travails of Kōichi, Noriko, and little Akiko just pale when considering the scope of destruction that Godzilla and company are capable of. Whereas the first film framed that destruction through the lens of the trio’s trauma, not just in regards to the giant monster but also specifically around what they went through in the war, that resonance is missing here.

In fact, the most interesting character in Minus Zero is perhaps the most under-served. Kanji Murakami, played by Min Tanaka, is a scientist whose work is key to battling the monsters this time around. He’s also kind of warped, with Tanaka getting one scene in particular that is a bit too spoilery to describe here, but is also a highlight of the film. As with Kōichi and Noriko, and indeed every character in the film, the war irrevocably changed his life, and the scientist is still struggling to cope with that reality while he works to prevent a pair of living A-bombs from doing even more damage to humankind.

Speaking of which, a much ballyhooed sequence first glimpsed in the trailer last spring involving Godzilla and the Statue of Liberty is certainly something to behold here. Toho has asked critics to not reveal the specifics of this particular scene in reviews, but suffice to say that it is both everything you’ve imagined and theorized about, and at the same time none of that at all. It does connect back to Tanaka’s character in one of his darkest moments, and as a result is one of the film’s most memorable incidents of Godzilla-on-human action.

But that brings me back once again to the feeling that kept bubbling up for me while watching Godzilla Minus Zero. Even as Godzilla sets upon what looks like Spider-Noir’s version of New York City, the whole emotional underpinning of the scene is tied to Tanaka’s Murakami. Unfortunately, the character’s true motivations and how they’re ultimately resolved in the film play as more of an after-thought than Minus Zero’s thematic or emotional core, and for that film suffers.

If there is a central theme at work here, it’s the idea that no matter how hard we as a species try, we can’t outrun our own mistakes – and we’re gonna keep making them over and over again, despite the efforts of the best among us. Minus One ended with a hint of what was next for Noriko; while she miraculously survived a Godzilla attack, she also now bore a mysterious scar on her neck from the experience. It’s no surprise to learn in Minus Zero that it was no mere scar, and that in fact Noriko is now also a very important player in the fight against the monsters. But she, like Kōichi, is also a pawn in a greater game that’s happening on the world stage involving the monsters. The regular folks on the ground are the ones bearing the trauma of the battles that have been fought, but the powers that be don’t seem to care…

By the final act, you know where this is all going, and that’s fine. Monsters must brawl, and as with Minus One, the period setting of this film really adds to the luster of the visual effects and action scenes. Seeing Kōichi back in the pilot seat, this time of 1949-era fighter planes, is thrilling, and the various schemes concocted by the returning Kenji Noda (Hidetaka Yoshioka), now the head of the “Large-Scale Disaster Response Bureau,” are often ingenious and satisfyingly crunchy in their attempts to slow down and ultimately stop Godzilla and his enemy.

articles.title: Star Wars Nabs Spider-Man Director Jon Watts for First Movie in Disney's New Skywalker Saga Trilogy
articles.summary: Disney has reportedly picked Spider-Man director Jon Watts to helm the first movie in Simon Kinberg's new Star Wars trilogy as it plots out the next chapter in the Skywalker Saga.
articles.body:
Disney has reportedly picked Spider-Man director Jon Watts to helm the first movie in Simon Kinberg's new Star Wars trilogy as it plots out the next chapter in the Skywalker Saga.

Information about a new series of Star Wars projects from Lucasfilm was first reported by Daniel Richtman and later corroborated by The Hollywood Reporter . Although Watts is best known for leading the charge on the Marvel Cinematic Universe's Tom Holland Spider-Man trilogy, his work on Star Wars would represent his return to the sci-fi franchise following his time as co-creator on 2024's Skeleton Crew .

The yet-to-be-named new films, which are said to be the next chapter in the Skywalker Saga, are being written by Star Wars: Rebels and Mr. and Mrs. Smith veteran Kinberg. Story details remain mostly shrouded in mystery, though it's said that Daisy Ridley's sequel trilogy Jedi, Rey Skywalker, will play a role in the story.

Watts has only been picked to direct the first movie of the new trilogy so far. When this next chapter will begin is also unclear, with The Hollywood Reporter sources noting that Disney has not given the new project the official green light as work on its foundation continues.

Although still early in development, the site stated that it is further along than most other Star Wars projects. The only one ahead of it for now is Shawn Levy and Ryan Gosling's Star Wars: Starfighter , which has a May 28, 2027, release date.

Watts broke onto the blockbuster scene with the MCU's Spider-Man: Homecoming in 2017 and returned to make more superhero movies with follow-ups Far from Home and No Way Home in 2019 and 2021, respectively. He then handed over work on future Holland films to Destin Daniel Cretton, with his last feature, Wolfs, premiering in 2024.

Kinberg was first said to be in the mix to write a new Star Wars trilogy back in 2024, but there was conflicting information at the time. While some reported the next run of mainline films would continue the Skywalker Saga, others stated that the new projects would tell a completely new story. The Hollywood Reporter's story today suggested that Kinberg has settled on the former, though with the project so early in development, it's always possible that could change.

Former Lucasfilm boss Kathleen Kennedy offered an update on Kinberg's status when speaking to Deadline earlier this year. Although it seemingly ran into a few speed bumps along the way, today's update suggests the trilogy may be in the process of finding its footing and, hopefully, a path toward a full green light.

"[Kinberg] wrote something that we read in August, and it was very good, but not there," she said in January. "We've pretty much upended the story, and then spent a great deal of time on the treatment, which he finished literally about four weeks ago. And it's a very detailed treatment, like 70 pages. And so he is expected to give us something in March."

How Much Every Star Wars Movie Made Opening Weekend

Talk to most Star Wars fans and they'll tell you the same thing: The franchise is not in the best shape at the moment – at least when it comes to its movies. The Skywalker Saga concluded a massive nine-film arc with its sequel trilogy ender, Episode 9 – The Rise of Skywalker, in 2019, but the project capped the story with more of a whimper than a bang.

Although the Ridley-led films each came with their own controversial moments, The Rise of Skywalker emerged with disappointing critical reception (IGN gave it a 7/10 ) rivaled only by 1999's Episode 1 – The Phantom Menace . Disney pumped the breaks when it came to theatrical releases for a galaxy far, far away after that, with this year's The Mandalorian and Grogu bringing an end to a seven-year drought without new Star Wars movies. Even that project found its own trials to overcome, with so-so critical reception (IGN's review delivered a 5/10 ) and underwhelming box office returns leading Disney to deem it a disappointment in theaters .

It's not all been doom and gloom for Star Wars, though. While the movies have, for many, struggled to recapture the magic of George Lucas' original vision, some of its TV outings have managed to keep audiences coming back for more. Seasons 1 and 2 of Disney's Rogue One prequel, Andor, earned the franchise critical acclaim . Meanwhile, although not everyone was sold on 2024's The Acolyte , shows like Maul – Shadow Lord and Skeleton Crew did manage to find dedicated audiences .

Star Wars is going through some growing pains as leadership shifts behind the scenes , but Disney has made it clear it still has plenty of stories to tell. There are plenty of other movies and shows in various forms of development , including Maul – Shadow Lord Season 2 and Ahsoka Season 2 , which are both expected to premiere next year. While fans are still campaigning to see Adam Driver reprise his role as Kylo Ren in the canceled Hunt for Ben Solo film , Lucasfilm head Dave Filoni has signaled a bright future ahead when it comes to Star Wars movies .

Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).
